collections.title: Multivariable Calculus · Foundations Survey
collections.summary: Multivariable differentiation, integration and geometry, with deeper routes through optimization, variational methods, compatible mixed elements, and elliptic boundary regularity.

collections.title: Local Models and Newton Methods · From Taylor Bounds to Convergence
collections.summary: Four worked studies: Taylor integral remainders and cubic error estimates; Hessian eigenvalue bounds and strong convexity; Newton corrections for systems and objectives; a proof of local quadratic convergence and safeguards.
assumed_background: Calculus of one variable, the multivariable chain rule and Hessian, eigenvalues of small symmetric matrices, and solving small linear systems.

collections.title: Nonlinear Least Squares · From Gauss–Newton to Inverse Problems
collections.summary: A four-lecture construction route: residual Jacobians and Gauss–Newton; damped steps and trust-region acceptance; singular-value identifiability and covariance; structured regularization, robust losses and statistical assumptions.
assumed_background: The multivariable chain rule and Jacobians, Taylor models and Newton corrections, linear least squares and singular values. Statistical assumptions are introduced explicitly.

collections.title: Constrained Newton and Sensitivity · From Feasible Geometry to Implicit Derivatives
collections.summary: Four constructive studies: second variation along equality constraints; active inequality cones and regularity; block Newton/KKT solves; implicit parameter derivatives, envelopes, and adjoints.
assumed_background: Jacobian and Hessian matrices; linear algebra of null spaces; Newton corrections; an introduction to Lagrange multipliers is helpful but not essential.

collections.title: Variational Methods and Weak PDEs · From First Variation to Finite Elements
collections.summary: Four construction-level studies: functional derivatives and exact energy minima; Euler–Lagrange and natural boundary terms; Sobolev weak solutions with an interface example; finite-element assembly, Galerkin orthogonality and exact error.
assumed_background: Single-variable integration by parts, elementary multivariable quadratic forms, matrix systems, and a willingness to learn the basics of weak derivatives and Hilbert spaces.

collections.title: Weak Compactness and Nonlinear Existence · From Sobolev Bounds to Free Boundaries
collections.summary: Four proof-and-example studies: weak versus strong convergence and energy loss; Sobolev compact embeddings and critical-scale concentration; direct-method existence and uniqueness for a nonlinear energy; a solved obstacle problem with its exact contact region.
assumed_background: Weak derivatives, integration by parts, L-two inner products and the energy principle; the first lecture revisits every main prerequisite.

collections.title: Mixed Finite Elements and Inf–Sup Stability · From Fluxes to Stokes Solvers
collections.summary: Four constructive lectures: mixed Poisson and a conservative two-cell solve; abstract saddle-point inf–sup and Schur complements; a failed two-cell pressure pair repaired with mesh-uniform stability; Stokes flow, stable pressure, block solvers and error estimates.
assumed_background: Weak integration by parts and the one-dimensional Poisson problem; finite-dimensional equality constraints; elementary FE basis functions. New spaces and the stability test are derived during the route.

collections.title: Traces, Elliptic Regularity and Corners · From Weak Data to Reliable Mesh Error
collections.summary: Four constructive lectures: endpoint traces and Dirichlet lifts; Neumann compatibility, gauges and Robin weak forms; interior H2 gain by difference quotients; a cutoff reentrant-corner solution disproving unconditional global H2 and limiting uniform-mesh rates.
assumed_background: One-dimensional integration by parts, basic H1 weak solutions, elementary Poisson equation and FEM error bounds; difference quotients and trace norms are built in these lectures.

collections.title: Elliptic Principles and Estimates · Comparison, Green Kernels, Energy, and Harnack
collections.summary: Four worked lectures: weak and classical comparison and quadratic barriers; the exact interval Dirichlet Green kernel, distributions and spectral inverse; global and local energy estimates with Caccioppoli; planar Poisson kernels, sharp Harnack bounds and their rough-coefficient analogues.
assumed_background: Weak Poisson equations, integration by parts, basic Dirichlet and Neumann conditions, Sobolev H-one spaces, divergence theorem and elementary Fourier/eigenfunction ideas; precise new estimates and sign conventions are derived.

collections.title: Elliptic Boundary Behavior and Regularity · Hopf, Harmonic Measure, Schauder, Calderón–Zygmund
collections.summary: Four detailed lectures: an annular barrier proof of strict Hopf boundary growth and a corner counterexample; harmonic measure via Brownian exit and an exact disk arc integral; C2-alpha Schauder estimates, cancellation, and coefficient-form counterexamples; W2p Calderón–Zygmund theory and an explicit bounded-source/unbounded-Hessian example.
assumed_background: The weak and strong maximum principles, basic Dirichlet problems, Poisson and Green kernels, weak derivatives, H2 estimates, Lp norms and elementary Fourier analysis; key new estimates and counterexamples are derived.

collections.title: Boundary Harnack, Capacity and Wiener Regularity · How Much of the Boundary Counts?
collections.summary: Four constructive lectures: boundary Harnack ratios on flat and wedge boundaries; energy capacity of balls and planar annuli; removable harmonic singularities and polar sets; Wiener’s dyadic capacity test including a concrete thin-obstacle irregular boundary.
assumed_background: Harmonic functions and their maximum principle, positive solution comparison, Dirichlet energy, weak solutions, Sobolev capacity, and Green/Poisson kernels; energy capacities and the point-removal barrier proof are developed here.
